696: 
697: In order to derive the rotation curves, we applied the tilted-ring 
698: modelling of the velocity field for NGC 1090. For the other galaxies we determined the kinematical 
699: centre and the systemic velocity by minimising the differences between the two
700: sides. The errors are the maximum of the three following values: the difference
701: between the velocities of the approaching and the receding sides, our correction for 
702: beam broadening of the profiles, and a ``minimum error'' 
703: equal to ($2/sin~i$) km s$^{-1}$.
704: 
705: The MET/WAMET rotation curve served as an input to 
706: construct model data cubes with the task GALMOD within GIPSY \citep{vdH:92}; 
707: these models
708: have been then compared to the observed data cubes. 
709: Such models are built with the assumption that the neutral hydrogen moves along
710: circular orbits; a series of geometrical and physical parameters, among which
711: the rotation curve, allows us to create model observations of the {H{\sc i}}
712: discs. These models, when compared to the real data cubes,
713: verify whether they are a fair representation of the {H{\sc i}} disc.
714: Some input parameters are inferred directly from the observations and
715: kept fixed (e.g., the
716: surface density profile), while others (e.g., the kinematical 
717: centre and the systemic velocity) are first estimated from the
718: observations and then adjusted in order to optimise the match between
719: the observed and the model cubes.
720: 
721: In two cases (ESO 287-G13 and NGC 1090, the galaxies with the steepest rotation curves) the 
722: rotation curve derived with MET/WAMET had to be slightly modified in order to better reproduce
723: the observed data cubes. We found out that it was necessary to increase the value of the 
724: rotation velocity of the 2--3 innermost 
725: points by values of the order of their $1~ \sigma$ error; this is probably due to the fact that,
726: even with the MET/WAMET method, when the rotation curve rises steeply we are not able
727: to retrieve precisely the true rotation velocity; this is however possible by modelling the data cube.
